chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Fadalah from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar said:

I saw the Servant (peace be upon him) enter the Ka'bah and pray two rak'ahs upon the red marble. Then he stood and faced the wall between the Yemeni corner and the Western corner, raised his hand against it, pressed it against it, and supplicated. Then he moved to the Yemeni corner, pressed against it, and supplicated. Then he went to the Western corner, then exited.

key_terms.اَلرُّخَامَةُ اَلْحَمْرَاءُ: The red marble, a specific material/area inside the Ka'bah
key_terms.اَلرُّكْنُ اَلْغَرْبِيُّ: The Western corner of the Ka'bah
key_terms.اَلرُّكْنُ اَلْيَمَانِيُّ: The Yemeni corner of the Ka'bah
key_terms.اَلْعَبْدُ: The Servant (a title for Imam al-Sadiq, peace be upon him)
key_terms.اَلْكَعْبَةُ: The Ka'bah, the cubic building in Mecca

ai.seo_question: What is the recommended etiquette and ritual actions for entering and praying inside the Ka'ah according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights the unique status of Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) by demonstrating his independent authority to enter the Ka'bah for prayer, a privilege historically restricted to the Prophet and, in some interpretations, the Imams. The specific detail of pressing his hand against the walls and corners during supplication underscores the Shia emphasis on the Ka'bah as a locus of divine connection and barakah, extending beyond mere circumambulation. This practice reinforces the theological view that the Imams possess a direct, spiritual link to the sacred geometry of the House of God.
